subject: Renewal + midcycle capacity bump — options and invoice split
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@medsprint.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + midcycle capacity bump — options and invoice split

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time last week — great context on your spike patterns for Q3. Per our conversation I attached three practical paths to cover the midcycle uplift while keeping your renewal co-term simple. Short summary: 

- Option A — Short burst top-up: one-off invoice for the extra capacity (no change to renewal). Fastest to implement, higher unit price.
- Option B — Staged annualize: amortize the uplift across remaining contract months; midterm charge is split across invoices, lowers monthly impact.
- Option C — Commit swap + credit: increase term commitment, give an onboarding credit in the quarter and lower per-token rate for the new committed units.

A few clarifying points:
- We can co-term the added capacity to your existing 12/31 renewal and annualize the uplift (Option B) if procurement prefers a single PO and predictable monthly invoicing.
- For legal: I attached an MSA excerpt showing billing windows and a sample amendment template.
- If Procurement wants invoice-splitting (partial Q3 invoice + pro-rated remainder on renewal), we can create a two-line invoice and mark the top-up as "temporary capacity" so it doesn't change list pricing.

Attached: MediSprint_Q3_Uplift_Options.pdf (proposal)

Ask: Which of the three options would you like to see priced formally? If Option B or C, I can produce a split-invoice quote for Procurement.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@medsprint.com>

Sean —

Appreciate the options. A couple quick questions from Procurement and Finance:

1) If we do Option B (amortize), can you show the exact invoice split by month and the net additional monthly committed spend? Finance wants to see the cashflow impact before sign-off.
2) For Option C, what level of discount are you able to offer on the additional committed units? We typically need a tangible delta vs one-off top-up to justify the longer-term commit.
3) Any compliance/contract implications if we change the commitment mid-term vs adding a schedule amendment?

Procurement is out until Friday but I wanted to get this to you early. If you can send a concrete quote and the PO language Procurement needs (two-line invoice example + amendment phrasing), that would speed things up.

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
Sr. Product Ops, MediSprint
alex.ramos@medsprint.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@medsprint.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsprint.com>
Date: 2026-07-24T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + midcycle capacity bump — options and invoice split

Alex —

Thanks — attached is a concrete quote workbook (20260724-MediSprint-quote.xlsx) with three tabs: invoice-split (Option B), top-up one-off (Option A), and commit-swap economics (Option C). High-level answers below: 

1) Invoice split (Option B): I modeled a three-month amortization for the uplift (Aug–Oct). The invoice shows: Aug partial invoice (40% of uplift), Sep (30%), Oct (30%) plus the normal usage line. Monthly cashflow increase is ~18% on top of your current committed spend for Aug–Oct in the example pricing — numbers in the invoice-split tab.

2) Discount for Option C: We can offer a blended rate that nets ~12% off the one-off top-up unit price if you increase committed units by 25% for the remainder of the contract. That requires a schedule amendment and an updated commitment table in the SOW.

3) Contract impact: administratively simple — amendment + schedule update. We won't change other MSA terms. For procurement we can produce a one-page amendment template (attached MSA-excerpt.pdf) and sample PO language that references the amendment and lists the two invoice line items if you want split invoicing.

Next steps I recommend: I can send a redlineable amendment + a finalized quote that maps to your PO lines. If Procurement wants to keep invoices identical month-to-month, choose Option C and we'll annualize immediately with the new committed units. If they need a shorter-term cashflow buffer, Option B is usually the preferred path.

Attached: 20260724-MediSprint-quote.xlsx (xlsx), MSA-excerpt.pdf (pdf)

If Procurement is OK with the 12% blended discount on the committed uplift, I'll start legal/CS handoffs and flag for a one-time onboarding credit to offset implementation effort.

Best,
Sean

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-27T15:22:00-07:00

Irene / Jordan — forwarding a short thread with MediSprint (see below). Procurement will likely request one of these paths. Highlights / ask: 

- They are leaning to either amortize the uplift over Aug–Oct (Option B) or convert to a commit swap (Option C).
- I modeled a 12% blended discount on the new committed units for Option C (25% uplift in committed units). That margin still keeps us within acceptable band given the uplift profile (see quote workbook).
- Proposal: approve a one-time onboarding credit up to $8k to help close (applied in Aug invoice) if Procurement pushes for a lower sticker.

Can you confirm if Legal needs to run special approval for the amendment language? Also need finance to approve the $8k onboarding credit and confirm whether we can show that as an invoice-level credit vs a discount (tax and AR impact).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min sync.

Best,
Sean
